transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark (Acme CTO), Sara (Lead ML Eng), Tom (Head of Security)

Summary (auto): quick scoping for POC comparing Hosted / Dedicated / Private for Acme Health's patient-assistant chat workloads. Will run benchmarks, define success criteria, and size dedicated capacity if needed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Samir, i'm the AE covering Acme, and with me is Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Mark: Good, thanks. We wanted to get through our compliance concerns early and also make sure we size this POC right.
[00:12] Priya: Great, thanks Mark. Can i just confirm the primary success criteria for you? last email said latency and data residency.
[00:20] Mark: Yeah latency, specifically p95 under 250ms for the patient assistant flow is the bar. second is that patient PHI never leaves the region and we have KMS-backed envelope encryption.
[00:32] Sara: Also want to validate quality doesn't regress more than a small delta vs our current model - like less than 3% drop on core intents. We'll provide eval prompts.
[00:42] Tom: From security, SOC2 and audit logs are required, and we need SSO/SAML for access plus RBAC. Also we'll want a runbook for data deletion.
[00:52] Samir: Perfect, that's helpful. Quick question on traffic - are you expecting steady traffic or spiky? what are the baseline numbers?
[01:00] Mark: For the POC we want to test two modes: a low-volume pilot at ~10k requests/month and an expected production profile of ~120k requests/month with peak windows that hit 600 qps for short periods.
[01:12] Priya: Okay that helps. For benchmarking we'll want representative traces and samples, ideally a histogram of sequence lengths. even token distributions would be super helpful so we can size KV cache and batching.
[01:25] Sara: i'll prepare 1k sample prompts and a traffic trace. we have a mix of short confirmations (10-20 tokens) and longer multi-turn transcripts (~200 tokens).
[01:35] Samir: on deployment modes - high level: Hosted is the fastest to try and lowest setup friction; Dedicated gives you isolated reserved capacity and predictable latency/cost; Private (VPC/on-prem) is for customers that need control over networking and full on-prem compliance.
[01:48] Mark: If hosted is easiest, why would we ever pick dedicated?
[01:52] Priya: Good q. Dedicated is recommended when you need predictable throughput and isolation, or when your peak concurrency would cause variability on shared infra. Also dedicated makes long-running KV cache and large batch tuning more effective. There's also contractual SLAs.
[02:06] Mark: And private is only if compliance won't allow outbound to managed infra?
[02:09] Tom: For us, private is interesting because of regional restrictions and some payer contracts that require on-prem processing. but private is heavier ops.
[02:18] Samir: Correct. Our typical pattern: start with Hosted to validate latency/quality quickly. If you hit throughput or cost issues, move to Dedicated pilot with reserved GPUs and autoscaling. Private is pursued only if compliance/legal blocks hosted/dedicated or you require on-prem.
[02:32] Sara: What's the effort to move from hosted to dedicated? any code changes?
[02:36] Priya: Minimal. Same API, same prompts. You can pin model versions and rollout policies. For Dedicated we'll need to size GPU pools - we'll ask for RPS, seq length distribution and model choice to recommend instance counts.
[02:48] Mark: model choice - are you recommending open models or something else?
[02:51] Priya: We recommend a curated set from our catalog; for conversational patient assistant we often start with a 8/16-bit quantized LLM variant that balances latency/cost. We'll suggest a few model profiles after we see samples.
[03:05] Tom: About encryption - can Redwood integrate with customer KMS?
[03:09] Samir: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Hosted can support per-tenant encryption at rest and in-transit but some customers require external KMS which is supported in Dedicated/Private.
[03:21] Mark: ok when can we run a benchmark?
[03:23] Priya: As soon as we have the 1k prompts and a small traffic trace - we can run an initial hosted benchmark in 1-2 business days. For a dedicated pilot sizing run we'll need the full expected production profile and a preferred model.
[03:33] Sara: we'll get the artifacts to you by Friday.
[03:36] Samir: Great. let's talk success criteria more concretely. we'll measure: p95 latency, tokens / second cost, and intent accuracy relative to your eval set. Does that cover it?
[03:46] Sara: yes, and also memory / kv cache hit rates would be useful to see.
[03:50] Priya: we'll instrument KV cache hit metrics and batch sizes in the benchmark report.
[03:56] Mark: any known limitations around multitenancy? we don't want cross-tenant degradation.
[04:02] Priya: In hosted we isolate at tenant level logically, but it's still shared infra. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools; Private gives you full isolation under your network. We'll provide tail-latency numbers from recent customers to help estimate.
[04:15] Tom: audit logs - can we get immutable audit trail for requests including redaction?
[04:21] Samir: Yes, we have request-level audit logs and configurable redaction rules. For Private we can ship logs to your SIEM.
[04:28] Mark: pricing ballpark? this is sensitive, but we need ranges to budget.
[04:32] Samir: i'll share ranges: hosted per-token and per-embedding cost; dedicated monthly reserved pools with discount tiers; private has licensing + infra costs. i'll put a concise pricing ranges doc in the follow-up.
[04:44] Sara: also want to run a quality guardrail test - can Redwood do eval harness comparing outputs?
[04:48] Priya: yes, we support evals; we can run batch evals against your prompts and compute accuracy/regression deltas. We'll include that in the benchmark report.
[04:58] Mark: timeline - you mentioned quick hosted test then dedicated pilot. what's realistic?
[05:03] Samir: Typical POC: 1 week to run hosted benchmark and analyze; 2-3 weeks for a dedicated pilot (provisioning, run full-scale test); total decision window about 4-6 weeks. If Private is required, add provisioning time - could be 6-10 weeks depending on infra and legal.
[05:19] Tom: who owns infra provisioning for private? us or Redwood?
[05:22] Priya: For Private we provide an on-prem package and config, but your infra team will handle hardware/network; Redwood assists with deployment and config. For VPC-private we can do a managed control plane with customer-managed networking.
[05:36] Samir: let's get specific on benchmarks: we'll run 3 phases - baseline hosted single-node p50/p95/p99, then scale tests to recreate your 600 qps peaks, and finally quality evals. We'll deliver a report with cost-per-1000-requests estimates.
[05:54] Sara: great. any gating items we should know?
[05:58] Priya: we'll need model selection, request trace, samples, and decision on whether you want to include embeddings/reranking in the POC. Those change resource use.
[06:08] Mark: we do reranking for some flows, maybe include one reranking flow.
[06:12] Samir: noted. Competitors - Mark, you mentioned you evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI, anything blocking?
[06:18] Mark: mostly cost and data residency concerns. also looking at Vertex AI for infra integration.
[06:24] Priya: we can run apples-to-apples latency/cost benchmarks vs a public baseline if helpful.
[06:30] Tom: SSO - we use Okta, SAML. Do you integrate?
[06:33] Samir: Yes Okta SAML is supported; we'll need your SSO admin to exchange metadata.
[06:41] Sara: For the dedicated sizing, what's typical GPU mix for 120k/month with 600 qps peaks for the model you recommended?
[06:48] Priya: ballpark: for a quantized model we might land on 2-4 A10s or 1-2 A100s for steady with burst autoscale; final rec requires the sequence-length histogram. We'll give a range in the sizing doc.
[06:59] Mark: If we start hosted and then switch to dedicated, is there a maintenance window?
[07:03] Priya: zero code changes; we move routing and capacity. There may be short cutovers but we support canary rollouts and traffic split.
[07:13] Samir: ok closing this up. we'll produce a follow-up email with attachments: pricing ranges, bench harness, security pack.
[07:20] Mark: can you include typical SLA numbers for dedicated?
[07:24] Samir: yes - I'll include 99.9/99.95 uptime ranges and latency SLO examples.
[07:30] Tom: also include list of compliance docs and SOC2 report.
[07:33] Samir: will do.
[07:36] Sara: one last Q - do you support bringing our own models into Redwood runtime?
[07:40] Priya: we support onboarding customer models for Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports curated models only for now. We'll outline the onboarding path.
[07:49] Mark: great. thanks everyone.
[07:51] Samir: thanks all. we'll send follow-ups.

Recap / Next steps (spoken):
- Acme to provide 1k sample prompts + request trace (Sara) by 2026-12-04.
- Redwood to run hosted benchmark within 1-2 business days of receiving samples and share report (Priya).
